bug_report:
Deep copy missing for allocatable derived type components
Consider the following minimal example:
```
program prog
    type node
        integer::val
        type(node),allocatable::next
    end type
    type(node)::a,b
    allocate(a%next)
    a%val=1
    a%next%val=2
    print*,a%val,a%next%val
    b=a
    b%val=3
    b%next%val=4
    print*,a%val,a%next%val
    deallocate(b%next)
    print*,a%val,a%next%val
end
```
The output of the code compiled with the GNU (gfortran-13.1.0) compiler is as follows:
```
           1           2
           1           4
           1           0
```
While the output of the code compiled with the Intel (ifx-2024.1.0) or NAG (nagfor-7.1) compiler is different:
```
           1           2
           1           2
           1           2
```

It seems like gfortran treats allocatable derived type components somewhat as pointers: after assignment `b=a`, the memory addresses of `a%next` and `b%next` are the same, and you can change `a%next%val` by changing `b%next%val`. However, deallocation of `b%next` will not deallocate `a%next` and will only change its content.

In contrast to this behavior, the Intel and NAG compilers perform a deep copy in the assignment `b=a` allocating new memory for elements of b.

The question to this example was asked here:https://stackoverflow.com/questions/78282004/are-allocatable-derived-type-components-just-pointers-for-gnu-compiler?noredirect=1#comment138008854_78282004and received an answer that this result is a bug of `gfortran`.
